question: At fixed inference and verifier budgets, does chronological discovery context increase independently verified strict bound improvement relative to the same history in a shuffled order?

arms.context: same prefix, identical blocks independently permuted
ordered prefix with verified lemma state; charge verification cost
ordered prefix, persistent recurrent state; compare with stateless D at matched compute

independent_unit: unseen mathematical problem family; descendants, variants, paraphrases and model repeats grouped by root
minimum_meaningful_effect: 1/20 absolute increase in independently verified strict improvement rate
match: source blocks and rendered token counts D/E
shams: E1 vs E2 independent matched shuffled prefixes; calibrate on at least 59 independent development families before confirmation; no use of DLMST as independent families
candidate: typed improvement with hypotheses, prior bound, proposed bound, derivation, and resource model; verifier returns pass/fail/unknown; unknown and budget exhaustion are failures
strict_improvement: prove f=o(g) in the stated common asymptotic regime; numeric finite-size tests alone do not qualify; preserve quantifier and computational-model fidelity

confirmation.seed_policy: custodian private, generate distinct structural families, commit root manifest before opening
confirmation.preflight: required before confirmation; exact paired McNemar only for independent binary roots; Holm/Bonferroni for registered contrasts; clustered uncertainty across families

exposure: DLMST and all 18 manuscripts public/reference-only. No public replay counts as held-out discovery. No model runs or held-out roots generated.
